text.title: LLM-Friendly Architecture (Software Developer) Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules every LLM-friendly architecture audit MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: The audit MUST report a line-count histogram over all source files and list every file above the line limit, sorted by size, each with a proposed split. The limit MUST be recorded in the artefact as an `inputs[]` entry `line_limit`; the default is 250 lines (the value `templates/llm-arch-audit.sh` uses) and it MUST NOT exceed 300. The decision names the specific files to split, never "reduce file sizes".

rationale.source: Methodology rubric (100-300 LOC per file); templates/llm-arch-audit.sh; widely established practice for agent-edited codebases

rule.rationale: A 1,400-line component is where AI edits go wrong: the model reads the top, edits the middle and breaks the bottom it never saw. The histogram turns "our files are big" into a ranked list, and the recorded limit is what makes next quarter's audit comparable to this one.

rule.statement: No source path MAY sit deeper than 3 directory levels below the source root (`src/a/b/c/file.ts` is the deepest allowed); feature folders are capped at 2 levels. The audit MUST list every violating path with its depth.

rationale.source: Methodology rubric (at most 3 directory levels); templates/claude-md-project.md structure section

rule.rationale: Every extra level is another `ls` an agent has to spend context on before it can find the file, and another place a parallel `utils/` grows. Flat trees are what let a model guess the right path from the name.

rule.statement: Barrel files (`export * from`, `index.ts` that only re-exports) are forbidden. The audit MUST list every barrel file found (the `llm-arch-audit.sh` barrel section) and imports MUST point at the module that defines the symbol.

rationale.source: templates/llm-arch-audit.sh (barrel re-export detection); Next.js documentation on `optimizePackageImports` and barrel-file cost

rule.rationale: A barrel hides where a symbol lives, so the agent opens `index.ts`, finds nothing, and either guesses or greps the whole tree. Bundlers dislike them for the same reason: `export *` defeats tree-shaking and makes every consumer pull the whole directory.

rule.statement: Wildcard imports are forbidden: `from x import *` in Python, `import * as` and namespace imports in TypeScript except for a documented allow-list. The audit MUST run an import lint (Ruff `F403`/`F405` for Python; `eslint-plugin-import` `import/no-namespace` or an equivalent rule for TypeScript) and list every hit.

rationale.source: Ruff rule documentation (F403, F405); eslint-plugin-import rule documentation (no-namespace); methodology rubric (explicit imports)

rule.rationale: A star import means the name the agent is about to use may or may not exist, and the only way to know is to open the other file. Explicit imports make every file self-describing in its first 20 lines, which is the part the model reads most carefully.

rule.statement: The naming-clarity score MUST be computed from a stated rubric (file name matches its primary export; kind-specific casing: PascalCase components, `use-*` hooks, kebab-case utils; no catch-all names such as `utils2`, `misc`, `helpers`, `common`, `stuff`; no unexplained abbreviations) and the audit MUST list the offending files, not only the score.

rationale.source: Martin, Clean Code (2008), ch. 2 'Meaningful Names'; templates/claude-md-project.md conventions section

rule.rationale: A score of 71/100 is not actionable; `helpers2.ts` is. Names are the only index an agent has before it reads a file, so `format-currency.ts` finds the right place in one guess and `utils.ts` in six.

rule.statement: Static literal data (arrays or objects of constants, copy, config tables) MUST live in `src/data/` (or the project's declared equivalent), never inline in components or route files. Route entry points stay orchestrators of roughly 30 to 50 lines. The audit MUST list components carrying inline data blocks.

rationale.source: templates/claude-md-project.md (data extracted to src/data/, pages as orchestrators)

rule.rationale: A 200-line array of menu items inside a component eats the file's line budget and the model's attention on every edit to the rendering logic. Moving data out is the cheapest split there is: it needs no refactor of behaviour and removes the largest block from the file.

rule.statement: A project `CLAUDE.md` (from `templates/claude-md-project.md`) MUST exist at the repo root and state the commands, the directory structure and the conventions the audit checks. The line limit written in `CLAUDE.md` MUST equal the `line_limit` used by the audit; a mismatch fails the audit.

rationale.source: Anthropic, 'Claude Code: Best practices for agentic coding' (CLAUDE.md as the project's standing instructions); methodology template claude-md-project.md

rule.rationale: The audit finds the violations; `CLAUDE.md` is what stops the agent from creating new ones tomorrow. When the two disagree (audit says 250, `CLAUDE.md` says 400) the model follows the file it reads on every session, and the audit becomes a quarterly complaint.

rule.statement: The audit MUST be produced by a committed script (`templates/llm-arch-audit.sh` or the project's equivalent) and the artefact's `evidence[]` MUST include the command run and the commit SHA it ran against. A hand-curated list of "big files" is rejected. The same command MUST run in CI on every pull request once the baseline is clean.

rationale.source: Widely established practice for lint-style checks; templates/llm-arch-audit.sh

rule.rationale: A one-off audit is a snapshot nobody reruns; three months later the files are back to 900 lines and the audit says everything is fine because nobody updated it. Pinning the command and SHA makes the audit a diff between two known states instead of an opinion.
